newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Luxembourg to issue EMU benchmark bond next year.
newsitem.headline: Luxembourg to issue EMU benchmark bond next year.

text.p: Luxembourg will start issuing its benchmark 10-year bond for European economic and monetary union (EMU) around April 1997, Treasury Director Yves Mersch said on Thursday.

Mersch told Reuters the issue would depend on passage of the country's 1997 budget through parliament and a new law to convert all existing Luxembourg state debt to euros once EMU takes place on January 1, 1999.
"I expect parliament will approve these by the beginning of next year," he said.

France, Belgium and Austria have all pledged to convert outstanding debt to euros in 1999. But under a bill proposed by the government in September, Luxembourg aims to be the first country to make such a pledge legally binding.
The Luxembourg Treasury said earlier this week that at its next auction on November 20 it would continue to offer the present 6.00 percent benchmark bond maturing in February 1996.
Under the Maastricht treaty, countries will be judged whether they are ready for EMU on the basis of a series of 1997 economic data, including their deficits, debt and currency stability.

The treaty also says EU members taking part in EMU must have long-term interest rates 150 basis points within the average of the three best performers measured in terms of price stability. A basis point is one hundredth of a percentage point.

Luxembourg, which has practically no deficit or national debt and is the only country to currently clearly meet all the Maastricht treaty criteria, only has a regular borrowing programme to meet this Treaty obligation.
The size of issues is very small and will remain so, Mersch said.
At last month's auction, the present 2006 benchmark was for the first time sold at a yield discount to German 10-year Bunds.
